 JUDGMENT This final report filed by the CCB OCW police station against the accused for the offences punishable U/s.406, 420, 120(b) r/w of IPC.

2. BRIEF FACTS :- Case of the prosecution is CW 5 and 6 are sons of CW.1 by name R. Prakash and Accused no.1 to 4 with common intention to commit crime made criminal conspiracy and for purpose to cheat the complainant with dishonest intention and assured to the complainant to provide police constable appointment to the CW 5 and Accused have received Rs.5,50,000/- amount from CW 1, there after without providing any appointment, Accused have deceived the complainant from the amount and accused have committed criminal breach of trust and induced the complainant to paid the amount.

C.C.No.15038/2019 3. Based on the information of CW-1, the police have registered the case, investigation was conducted and after completion of the investigation, charge sheet filed against the accused no. 1 to 4 stating that they have committed the aforesaid offences.
4. The accused no.1 to 4 have entered appearance in response to the summons and has been enlarged on bail.
The prosecution papers has been supplied to the accused no. 1 to 4.
After hearing the charge is read over and explained to the accused to which they pleaded not guilty and claims to be tried.

5. The prosecution has examined CW.5 and CW.6 as PW 1 and 2 and Ex.P.1 and 2 document are exhibited.
6.
The statement under Sec.313 of Cr.P.C., was dispensed because, there is no incriminating evidence against accused no.1 to 4.
Further CW 1 reported to dead.
CW 5 and 6 examined they being sons of CW 1 examined as PW 1 and 2 and got marked Ex.P.1 and 2 documents.
Admittedly, CW 1 who is C.C.No.15038/2019 father of CW 5 and 6 has been died and Accused have paid the amount of Rs. 4,50,000/- to the PW 1 and 2 as per their evidence and order sheet.

Of course CW 7 to 10 appears to be victims as per charge sheet but Accused no. 1 to 4 submits have not received any amount from them, accordingly, due to compromise of dispute between the victims PW 1 and 2 and Accused
, on examination of other charge sheet witness no purpose of prosecution case will survives.
Hence by rejecting the prayer of Ld. APP.
Evidence of other witness is taken as given up.
In the absence of incriminating evidence 313 Cr.P.C statement is dispensed.
Heard on both sides.
7. Heard the arguments. Perused the documents on record.

8. The following points that arise for my consideration:-

sentences.text:
1. Whether the prosecution proves beyond reasonable doubt CW 5 and 6 are sons of CW 1 by name R. Prakash and Accused no. 1 to 4 with common intention to commit crime made criminal conspiracy and for purpose to cheat the complainant with dishonest intention and assured to the complainant to provide police constable appointment to the CW 5 and Accused have received received Rs.
5,50,000/- amount from CW 1, there after without providing any appointment Accused have deceived the complainant from the amount and accused have committed criminal breach of trust and induced the complainant to paid the amount and thereby committed an offence punishable U/sec. 406, 420, 120(b) r/w 34 of IPC?
2. What order?
9. For the reasons to be stated herein after, I answer the above points as follows:

Point No.1 - In the Negative  Point No.2 - As per the final order  for the following:-
 C.C.No.15038/2019  REASONS 10. Point No.1:- In the instant case PW.1and PW.2 are the complainant sons who have testified that they do not know anything about this case.
That their father has not given the complaint and they have not given the statements as per Ex.P.1 and Ex.P.2 in this regard.

Further PW.1 and PW.2 plead ignorance to the contents of Ex.P.1 and Ex.P.2 and PW.1 and 2 have turned hostile and cross-examined by the Ld.Sr.APP wherein nothing substantial is elicited in order to support the case of prosecution.
11. During the course of arguments Ld.Sr.APP and accused no. 1 to 4 counsel argued as per the evidence and prays to dispose the case.

12. Further admittedly this case arise out of the complaint given by the complainant and the Investigation Officer filed charge sheet for the alleged offences and after framing the charge due to settlement C.C.No.15038/2019 of dispute between the complainant and accused, the complainant has turned hostile and in spite of cross- examination by the Ld.Sr.APP, PW.1 and PW.2 have not supported the prosecution case.
So in the absence of incriminating evidence the other evidence of charge sheet witnesses is taken has dropped by rejecting the prayer of Ld.Sr.APP.

Because on examination of other charge sheet witnesses, that too in the absence of incriminating evidence, in the evidence of PW.1 and PW.2 no purpose of prosecution case will survives, so in order to save the very precious time of this court and due to compromise of dispute between the parties, this court is Siddappa vs Mahadeviah on 1 April, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/119903343/
3 the opinion that the evidence of other witnesses is not at all requires, accordingly by rejecting the prayer of Ld.APP the evidence of remaining witnesses taken as nil and in the absence of incriminating evidence, the statement U/s.313 of Cr.P.C is dispensed with and then case is posted for arguments.
C.C.No.15038/2019 13.

Further this court was of the opinion that PW.1 and PW.2 are the material witness who has compromised with the accused no. 1 to 4 and therefore the remaining witnesses were dropped by rejecting the prayer of Ld.Sr.APP.
14.
On considering the evidence of PW.1 and PW.2 and Statements at Ex.P.1 and Ex.P.2, the evidence of PW.1 and PW.2 appears to be contradictory.
The evidence of PW 1 and 2 is inconsistent with Ex.P.1 and Ex.P.2.
PW.1 and 2 admitted to have compromised with the accused no. 1 to 4.
That means as per evidence and ordersheet PW.1 and PW.2 have received settlement amount Rs.4,50,000/- from accused.
Hence they turned hostile.
Therefore, I hold that the prosecution is unable to establish the guilt of the accused no. 1 to 4 beyond reasonable doubt.
Hence, the accused deserves to be C.C.No.15038/2019 acquitted.
Therefore, I answer points No.1 in the NEGATIVE.
15. Point No.2:

From the discussions on foregoing points, this court opined that prosecution has failed to establish the guilt of the accused no. 1 to 4 punishable under the alleged sections 406, 420,
120(b) r/w 34 of Indian Penal Code.

Therefore, I proceed to pass the following:
ORDER Accused no. 1 to 4 are not found guilty.
Acting U/s.248(1) Cr.P.C., I hereby ACQUIT the accused of the offences punishable U/sec. 406, 420, 120(b) r/w.34 of IPC.
The bail bond of the accused no. 1 to 4 stands cancelled.
The cash security offered by accused no. 1 to 4 for their release on bail shall be refunded on proper identification, after appeal period is over.
